title: Where does unsafe begin?
subtitle: Pick an operation to see if it needs unsafe and what you must guarantee

layers.safe: Safe Rust · the compiler proves it

index.label: Index a Vec
index.text: Bounds are checked at runtime: an out-of-range index panics, it never reads foreign memory. Use get(i) to get an Option instead.

rawCreate.label: Create a raw pointer
rawCreate.text: Creating, copying, comparing or printing a raw pointer is safe. A pointer is just an address until someone dereferences it.

intToPtr.label: Cast an integer to a pointer
intToPtr.text: Also safe: the result may be dangling or misaligned, but holding it is harmless. The danger begins at the dereference.

forget.label: Leak memory
forget.text: Surprisingly safe. Leaks cannot cause undefined behaviour, so mem::forget and Box::leak are safe functions. Memory safety ≠ no leaks.

deref.label: Dereference a raw pointer
deref.text: The pointer must be non-null, aligned, point to a live and initialized value of that type, and must not violate aliasing: no live &mut to the same place while you read or write through it.

unsafeFn.label: Call an unsafe fn
unsafeFn.text: The caller must uphold the function's documented preconditions. For get_unchecked(i): i < len, otherwise it reads out of bounds.

staticMut.label: Mutate a static mut
staticMut.text: No other thread may access it at the same time, and no reference to it may be alive. In edition 2024 references to static mut are rejected: prefer atomics, Mutex or &raw mut.

union.label: Read a union field
union.text: The bytes currently stored must be a valid value of the field's type. Reading an f32 union field as a bool could produce an invalid bool, which is undefined behaviour.

unsafeImpl.label: Implement Send/Sync manually
unsafeImpl.text: You promise the type really is safe to move or share between threads. The compiler will trust this promise everywhere the type is used.

ffi.label: Call a C function
ffi.text: The declared signature must match the C side exactly, and every pointer you pass must satisfy the C function's contract (valid, NUL-terminated, large enough, not freed twice).

stillChecked: Inside an unsafe block the borrow checker, type checker and lifetimes still run as usual. unsafe only unlocks the operations above.
